recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No further core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-21284 unless a new work-group decision asks for additional core narrative or examples; future definition wording changes belong in the FHIR Extension Pack.
issue_request: FHIR-21284 was Published/Persuasive and requested two extensions, targetElement and targetPath, to identify a specific element in a referenced target resource. The accepted resolution specified targetElement as a valueUri containing the target element id, targetPath as a valueString containing simplified FHIRPath, and clarified that the extensions should apply to Reference datatype instances generally rather than only Provenance.target.
initial_application: Core commit 38993a71efdea21922d51b0ba140af67cc084cec explicitly applied FHIR-21284 by adding the reference extensions spreadsheet and fhir.ini registration, including targetElement and targetPath rows for Reference. Commit b84bf92092849d997f7f5edd3a15e75305fe8d55 added Provenance examples using the new extensions. A March 2022 FHIR-I Zulip thread recorded that the extension pages and Provenance examples were present and presumed sufficient.
additional_context: Core commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 later removed extension definitions from R5 core source as part of the extension move to the FHIR Extension Pack. The current Extension Pack definitions preserve the canonical URLs, Reference context, and uri/string value types; later FHIR-27877 expanded the same extension family to Reference/canonical, and related Provenance guidance issues FHIR-23076 and FHIR-48368 are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current core checkout should not duplicate Extension Pack-owned targetElement/targetPath definitions, and active core Provenance narrative/examples already point implementers to those extensions.
